name: Kathleen Walker

bio.statement: Walker's pamphlet statement lists prior governmental experience as Sandy Mayor 2025-present, Sandy City Council 2021-2024, and the Sandy Parks Board and Budget Committee.
bio.excerpt: Sandy Mayor: 2025-present; Sandy City Council: 2021-2024; Sandy Parks Board and Budget Committee

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 50 (printed C-49)

verification.note: Candidate-furnished pamphlet listing, not an official roster. Pronoun-free rewrite (candidate states no pronouns).

bio.statement: Walker's pamphlet statement lists Mt. Hood National Forest recreation manager (1992-2015) and forest planner (1983-1992), and a forestry degree from Colorado University.
bio.excerpt: Mt. Hood National Forest: Recreation Manager 1992 2015; Forest Planner 1983-1992; Educational Background: Colorado University, Forestry, BS

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 50 (printed C-49)

verification.note: Statement mentioned a forestry degree not in the excerpt; excerpt extended to include the education line. Pronoun-free rewrite (candidate states no pronouns).

positions.statement: Walker's pamphlet statement says developers must pay their share of system development charges when building.
positions.excerpt: Developers must pay their share of system development charges (SDCs) when building!

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 50 (printed C-49)

positions.statement: Walker's pamphlet statement says Walker will work to find more grant funding in Salem and D.C. to lower utility bills.
positions.excerpt: More grants can lower our utility bills. Last year, I helped get Sandy $6 million in government grants for our wastewater projects. I will work tirelessly to find more grant funding in Salem and D.C.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 50 (printed C-49)

verification.note: Statement says grants would lower costs; excerpt extended to include the sentence that says so; 'Washington D.C.' shortened to 'D.C.' as printed. Pronoun-free rewrite (candidate states no pronouns).

positions.statement: Walker's pamphlet statement says Walker will seek additional funding, without raising the safety fee, to expand the future police force.
positions.excerpt: I’ll seek additional funding that doesn’t raise our safety fee, to expand our future police force.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 50 (printed C-49)

positions.statement: Walker's pamphlet statement includes reducing high density growth in a list introduced with 'As Mayor I focused on'.

source.publisher: Clackamas County Elections, Official Voters' Pamphlet (Nov 3, 2026), PDF p. 50 (printed C-49)

verification.note: Original said the item is among Walker's mayoral focuses; the list is introduced in the past tense ('As Mayor I focused on'), so the wording now says so. Pronoun-free rewrite (candidate states no pronouns).

positions.statement: On the Walker campaign website, Walker says Walker will work to manage and control growth if elected mayor.
positions.excerpt: If elected as Mayor, I will work to manage and control growth.

verification.note: Campaign letter is undated, references Walker's November 2019 council election and says 'If elected as Mayor'; Walker's own pamphlet lists mayoral service from 2025 and a Sandy Post article (2024-08-09) shows Walker ran for mayor in 2024, so the page appears to be a 2024 campaign letter, not 2026 material. Cannot be dated or labelled reliably.
